lateFiler.name: Bruiser
lateFiler.flavor: Slow, wide and hard to move. Walks through what it can.

shredder.name: Scrapper
shredder.flavor: Quick, thin and in a hurry. Gone before you have aimed.

finalNotice.name: Buckethead
finalNotice.flavor: Plated head to foot. Whatever you hit it with, hit it harder.

politician.name: The Politician
politician.flavor: Here to listen. Here to help. Here to take a percentage.

directReport.name: Underling
directReport.flavor: Carrying everything. Deciding nothing. There are always more.

middleManager.name: Middle Manager
middleManager.flavor: Holds a clipboard. Has never filled one in.

theDevil.name: The Devil
theDevil.flavor: Carries nothing. Signs everything. Someone else will handle it.

pompom.name: Pom-Pom
pompom.flavor: Never stops smiling. Never stops moving. Never, ever stops.

longsnap.name: Long Snapper
longsnap.flavor: One job. Does it perfectly. Has not been thanked since 2009.

catcher.name: The Catcher
catcher.flavor: Full pads, full squat, full commitment. Blocks everything you throw.

zamboni.name: Zamboni Wraith
zamboni.flavor: Resurfaces the ice. Resurfaces the grass. Resurfaces you.

unicornBoss.name: The Rainbow Reaper
unicornBoss.flavor: The mascot they were told not to book. Every colour of the spectrum, and all of them mean it.
unicornBoss._artFacing:
DRAWN FACING RIGHT, and this said 'left' until it was checked against the pixels. THAT IS THE REPORTED BACKWARDS BOSS. `mirroredFor` flips a sprite exactly when its heading disagrees with the way its art was drawn, so a wrong declaration here inverts the answer everywhere: the Rainbow Reaper walked the whole of level 3 back to front. She was reported as the LEVEL 1 boss, which is level 1's Politician -- he is drawn facing right, declared right, and is correct; the unicorn is level 3's, and is the one that was wrong.
HOW IT GOT WRONG: she arrived in the same upload as Pom-Pom, the Long Snapper, the Catcher and the Zamboni Wraith, and all four of THOSE really are drawn facing left. Hers was filled in with theirs. Nothing in the engine could have caught it -- which way a picture faces is not derivable from the picture -- so the only check is looking, and all eighteen enemy sprites were looked at when this was fixed. The other seventeen agree with their declarations.

touristSmall.name: Day Tripper
touristSmall.flavor: Two hours here, four hours back, one photo of a thumb.

touristMid.name: Tour Guide
touristMid.flavor: Holds the map. Holds the flag. Has not read either.

touristBig.name: The Overpacker
touristBig.flavor: Packed for every season, and it is only Tuesday.

tinyGlitch.name: Tiny Glitch
tinyGlitch.flavor: A rounding error with a sword. There is never one of them.

glitchBug.name: The Glitch Bug
glitchBug.flavor: An unhandled exception with wings. It has found your most expensive tower.

glitchBugBeta.name: Glitch Bug (Beta)
glitchBugBeta.flavor: An early build of the thing that is coming. Ships without the dangerous half.

glitchLich.name: The Glitch Lich King
glitchLich.flavor: Corrupted, crowned, and still rendering. Parts of him are from a different game.

glitchLichReturn.name: The Glitch Lich King
glitchLichReturn.flavor: He went away and recompiled. It did not improve his mood.

thrall._level5:
WHERE LEVEL 5'S SIX BEGIN, and this note is on the Thrall's row rather than at the top of the file because enemies.json is a FLAT MAP OF ENEMIES: every id in it is walked by the content, rules and wave tests as an enemy, and a top-level `_level5` key was read as one with no sprite and no tier. So the documentation lives inside a row, where an enemy's own `_` fields already live.
THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THEIR NAMES LIVE. `name` and `flavor` on the six rows from here down -- thrall, glider, babyFrank, vampireElite, vampireLord, batula -- are what the HUD, the boss bar and every log line print, and nothing else holds a copy. Renaming them for the kids is six edits here and nothing else. src/data/level5.json's `roster` lists which id plays which part.
FOUR OF THEM SHARE ONE SCALE. The Thrall, the Glider, the Elite and Baby Frank were cut from one sheet at one scale, so their sizes relative to each other are the artist's and are not re-chosen: art.json puts them on screen at 76.2, 74.2, 85.0 and 54.7, which is that one sheet multiplied by a single number. The Lord and Batula came separately and are sized against the roster.
THREE FIELDS ARE NEW WITH THIS LEVEL and no enemy above carries any of them: `vampiric` (the sun burns it and the night speeds it up), `lifesteal` (the share of the damage it deals to a player unit that it heals for) and `glides` (it hovers, so ground effects miss it). What each of them MEANS is in level5.json, which only level 5 names, so nothing here can reach levels 1 to 4.
thrall.name: Thrall
thrall.flavor: A villager, halfway through a career change. Still has the ears to grow into.
thrall._transform: NOT A VAMPIRE YET, which is why it carries neither `vampiric` nor `lifesteal`: the sun does not burn it, the night does not speed it up, and it heals off nothing. What happens to it instead is the dusk flip -- level5.json's `conversions` turns every live Thrall into a Glider where it stands, keeping its health as a PERCENTAGE, so one on its last sliver does not heal to full by changing.

glider.name: Glider
glider.flavor: Does not fly. Hovers, drifts, and is extremely smug about the distinction.
glider._layer: THERE IS NO `layer` HERE AND THERE MUST NOT BE. A Glider is not an air unit: every tower may shoot it, and putting it on the air layer would make it invisible to the ground-only Mortar and hand the level to whoever drafted the right gun. `glides` is a different question -- what it is out of reach OF, which is things lying on the ground -- and level5.json's `gliding` says what that means.
glider._attackInterval: 1.05, AND IT IS THE SURVIVAL FLOOR AGAIN. Three Gliders is what `blockCapacity` lets onto the hero at once and armor.test.ts asks that he last ten seconds under them: at 12 damage every 0.9s that is 40 a second and Cory is down in 9.0. At 1.05 it is 34.3 and he lasts 10.5. The Glider is also the enemy this matters most for, because it HEALS for half of what it deals -- a hero it is chewing through is a hero paying for the privilege.

babyFrank.name: Baby Frank
babyFrank.flavor: Six weeks old, four hundred volts, no supervision whatsoever.
babyFrank._speed: 172 IS THE FASTEST THING IN THE GAME and is meant to be. The Tiny Glitch held that at 140 and the Scrapper before it at 122, so this is 23% clear of the previous record rather than a tie -- a threat the brief describes as `the speed threat` has to be visibly faster than anything a player has already seen. It is not a vampire and the sun does not touch it.

vampireElite.name: Vampire Elite
vampireElite.flavor: Old money, older blood, and a coat that costs more than your tower.
vampireElite._attackInterval: 2.4, SET BY THE HERO'S SURVIVAL FLOOR rather than by feel. armor.test.ts asks that Cory last ten seconds with `blockCapacity` of the heaviest rank-and-file attacker on him at once, and three Elites is what this level actually puts there. At 26 damage every 1.8s that is 43.3 damage a second and he is gone in 8.3; at 2.4 it is 32.5 and he lasts 11.1. The damage per swing is left alone deliberately -- a heavy slow attacker should hit hard and rarely, and it is the RATE that was wrong.

vampireLord.name: Vampire Lord
vampireLord.flavor: Arrives with an entourage. Leaves as one.
vampireLord._tier: `tier` IS elite AND `role` IS boss, and the two disagree on purpose. `tier` is what the RULES read: only elites and bosses drop a Server Nuke, and only a `boss` tier gets the bar across the top of the screen -- and two Lords arrive together at wave 11, so a boss bar would have to pick one of them and would look like a bug. `role` is what a reader and the draft read, and this is a mini-boss.
vampireLord._livesCost: 4, AND IT IS CAPPED BY A RULE ABOUT THE RANK AND FILE. rules.test.ts asks that the starting purse of lives be at least five times the worst NON-BOSS leak, and this row is `tier: elite` -- deliberately, see `_tier` -- so it counts as rank and file for that sum. Twenty lives over five is four. Five would have quietly made the rule fail for every level in the game, not just this one.

batula.name: Batula
batula.flavor: Half bat, half vampire, entirely mortified. Please do not look directly at him.
batula._blockable:
THE FIRST BOSS IN THIS GAME THAT THE LINE CAN HOLD, and it is a decision rather than an oversight. Every boss before him is `blockable: false` for the reason the Politician's note gives: holding one lets a player park it and ignore the fight. Batula cannot be parked, because holding him is how he wins. He hits for 55 every two seconds and heals for ALL of it, so a line that stops him is a line feeding him -- the counterplay is bleed, which switches the healing off, and bleed only lands if somebody is shooting him. A boss who walked through the line would never bite anything and his lifesteal, which is the whole point of the level, would never once come up.
HE IS ALSO SLOWABLE, unlike the Rainbow Reaper. Hers is a clock -- she disables a tower every seven seconds whatever she is doing -- so a permanent slow turns her fight off. His clock runs on MOVEMENT: a slowed Batula covers less ground and therefore drops fewer puddles, which is a real reward for slowing him rather than an exploit, and a stopped one stops dropping them altogether and starts eating whatever stopped him.
batula._health:
4500, AND IT CAME OFF THE SOAK RATHER THAN OUT OF THE BRIEF -- which deliberately does not specify it, because a boss's health only means anything against the DPS the board it walks past can hold. The sensitivity table is in reports/2026-09-07-level-5.md: 3000 pays 51%, 3600 48%, 4200 43%, 4500 40%, 4800 33%, 5400 26%, 6000 23% at 120 seeds, one value at a time with the file reverted between rows. It is steep and monotonic, so HP genuinely controls this fight -- a flat table would have meant something else did. Confirmed at 480 seeds: 4400 gives 42%, 4500 40%, 4600 40%. 4500 is the middle of the 35-45% band.
THIS NUMBER IS NOT COMPARABLE TO LEVEL 4'S BOSS. Level 4 covers 45.3% of its tail with pads and this level covers 85.4% of its whole route, so the DPS a board can bring to bear is not the same quantity on the two of them -- and level 4's own figure was tuned against a simulator that did not model support auras.

scrapper._level6:
WHERE LEVEL 6'S FOUR BEGIN, and this note is on a row rather than at the top of the file for the reason the Thrall's gives: enemies.json is a flat map and every top-level key in it is walked as an enemy.
THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THEIR NAMES LIVE. `name` and `flavor` on the four rows from here down -- scrapper, sprinter, bruiser, rooster -- are what the HUD, the boss bar and every log line print. Rename them here and nowhere else.
THE GREY IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE JOKE. Level 6 is an unfinished level that knows it: white primitives, a wireframe unicorn, a blank billboard, a workman holding a sign reading `Are we out of ideas?`. The three rank and file are untextured mannequins with two dots for eyes, and the Rooster is the only finished thing in the level. Do not tint them, do not detail them, do not `fix` them.
scrapper.name: Scrapper
scrapper.flavor: Grey. Featureless. Two dots for eyes. Somebody ran out of time and it shows.

sprinter.name: Sprinter
sprinter.flavor: The same mannequin, in a hurry. Nobody told it the level was not finished.
sprinter._speed: 150 AND IT IS THE FASTEST THING IN THE GAME, which is the point of it. The order behind it is level 5's Baby Frank at 172 -- so this is NOT the fastest, and that is a conflict the brief could not have known about, because Baby Frank did not exist when it was written. See reports/2026-09-07-level-6-roster-and-plate-spec.md: the brief asks for the fastest unit in the game at 150 and level 5 shipped a 172 an hour earlier. Nothing here has been changed to resolve it; the number is the brief's and the collision is reported.

bruiser6.name: Bruiser
bruiser6.flavor: Twice the polygons, still no texture. It is very proud of the polygons.
bruiser6._id: `bruiser6` AND NOT `bruiser`, because `lateFiler` is already called Bruiser on screen -- level 1's first enemy, `name: "Bruiser"`, shipped months ago. Two rows may share a NAME (the Glitch Lich King has two) but not an id, and renaming level 1's would rename an enemy players have already met. The id is the one this file uses; the name is the one the kids see.
bruiser6._displayHeight: DRAWN AT 85 AND NOT THE 92 THE BRIEF ASKED FOR, in art.json. Every tower in the game is 87.1 px tall and content.test.ts holds the rank and file under that, so a 92 px Bruiser would be the only ordinary enemy on the board taller than every building on it.
bruiser6._attackInterval: 1.85 AND NOT THE BRIEF'S 1.5, and the number was set by a rule rather than by feel. armor.test.ts asks that Cory survive ten seconds with `blockCapacity` of the heaviest rank-and-file attacker on him at once, and three Bruisers is what this level actually puts there. At 22 damage every 1.5s that is 44 a second and he is gone in 8.2; at 1.85 it is 11.9 a second each and he lasts 10.1. The damage per swing is the brief's and is untouched -- a heavy slow attacker should hit hard and rarely, and it was the RATE that broke the floor. 11.89 dps also lands him level with the Overpacker's 11.88, which is the heaviest thing in the game before him.

rooster.name: The Rooster
rooster.flavor: The only thing in this level anybody finished. It has noticed, and it is furious.
rooster._maxHealth:
NULL ON PURPOSE, AND A TEST FAILS IF THIS LEVEL IS SHIPPED WITH IT STILL NULL.
A boss's health only means anything against the DPS the board it walks past can hold, and level 6's board does not exist yet -- its plate is a 2970x316 proof at contact-sheet resolution and has to be re-rendered before a single pad can be placed. Level 6 will be by a wide margin the largest board in the game: 2.3x the length with two full-length lanes, so substantially more than the 14 or 15 pads levels 2 to 5 carry. A number guessed now would be measured against a board with a different number of guns on it, which is exactly how level 4's boss came to be tuned against a simulator where the Beacon aura did nothing.
So it stays null until the map pass soaks it, and `tests/level6.test.ts` refuses to let levels.json name a level whose wave table spawns an enemy with no health.
rooster._damage: 0, and he is `blockable: false`, so he is the unholdable-and-harmless kind of boss the roster already has three of. What he does instead is the flame -- see level6.json's `flame` -- which is a line ahead of him along his own lane rather than a melee swing, so there is nothing for the line to hold and nothing for him to bite.

intern._level8:
WHERE LEVEL 8'S SIX BEGIN, and this note is on a row rather than at the top of the file because enemies.json is a flat map and every top-level key in it is walked as an enemy.
THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THEIR NAMES LIVE. `name` and `flavor` on the six rows from here down -- intern, hr, consultant, manager, officeDrone, ceo -- are what the HUD, the boss bar, the wave card and every log line print. Rename them here and nowhere else; nothing in src/ spells an enemy's name.
THE JOKE IS THE OFFICE. Level 8 is an abandoned corporate floor being optimised by the robots that replaced everybody, and every unit in it is an office robot with a lanyard. The Consultant's parting recommendation hurts its own side. Human Resources protects the people around it and is the thing you kill first. Middle Management is a golf club with a robot attached. None of that is a mechanic that needs softening.
intern._peanutReward: 13 AND NOT THE BRIEF'S 8, and the same 1.6x went on Human Resources, the Consultant and Middle Management -- the brief called its rewards starting values for the soak and this is what the soak said. LEVEL 8 HAS THE LARGEST BOARD IN THE GAME, 19 pads against levels 2 to 6's 15, 15, 14, 14 and 18, and the briefed rewards sat at the house MEDIAN of about 0.12 peanuts per point of enemy health -- which funds about ten towers over thirteen waves and leaves half the board empty. At the briefed numbers the level soaks at 0% over 20 seeds and the simulated player never reaches the CEO with lives left; at 1.6x it soaks in the 35-45% band. The four rows now pay 0.125 to 0.2 per point of health, which sits between levels 1 to 4 (0.08 to 0.13) and level 6 (0.27 to 0.44) rather than outside the game. EVERY OTHER LEVER WAS TRIED FIRST and the table is in reports/2026-09-12-level-8.md: halving every wave count moves the win rate from 0% to 0%, the HR aura moves it from 0% to 0%, and nothing but the purse moves it at all.
intern.name: The Intern
intern.flavor: Unpaid, uninsured, and moving at 145 pixels a second. Nobody told it what the job is.

hr.name: Human Resources
hr.flavor: Here to help. Has never once been here to help.
hr._armorAura: PROPOSED, NOT SETTLED -- the brief asks for it to be built and flagged, and it is flagged here and in the report. The flag is a boolean and the numbers are in level8.json's `armorAura` block, which is the scoping the Rooster's `flame: true` uses: `levelRules` returns null everywhere else, so an HR on another level would project nothing. Killing HR first makes everything around it easier, which is the whole design.
hr._attackInterval: 1.0, AND IT IS EXACTLY ON THE SURVIVAL FLOOR. armor.test.ts asks that Cory last ten seconds with `blockCapacity` of the heaviest rank-and-file attacker on him: 12 damage a second x 3 against 360 health is 10.0s exactly. Anything shorter than 1.0 here fails that test, and it is the reason the Consultant and Middle Management below do not carry the intervals the brief asked for.

consultant.name: The Consultant
consultant.flavor: Bills by the hour, explains what you already told it, and detonates on the way out.
consultant._deathBlast: IT DAMAGES BOTH SIDES and that is the joke, not a bug to fix. Radius and damage are in level8.json's `deathBlast` block; the boolean is here because exploding is a fact about the Consultant and the numbers are the level's. It reuses the existing area-damage path rather than adding one.
consultant._attackInterval: 1.25 AND NOT THE BRIEF'S 1.1. At 15 damage the brief's interval is 13.6 damage a second, and three of those on Cory kills him in 8.8s against armor.test.ts's ten-second floor. 1.25 is 12.0 a second, which is the floor exactly and is what Human Resources above also sits on. The damage number is the brief's and is the one a player reads.
consultant._role: `basic`, NOT `armored`, AND REGISTERING LEVEL 8 IS WHAT FOUND IT. Its wave table only entered tests/rules.test.ts's per-level checks the day level 8 got a row, and the first thing those checks said was that level 8 fields no `basic` at all: the Intern is `fast`, HR is `support`, and the Consultant and Middle Management were both `armored`. A level owes its player a basic, a fast and an armoured, and this row is the one that was mislabelled -- roles are about WHAT ANSWER THE BOARD NEEDS, and 6 armour needs no particular punch where Middle Management's 14 does. The Consultant is level 8's ordinary body: mid health, mid speed, arrives in numbers, and explodes. Nothing about it changed but the word.

manager.name: Middle Management
manager.flavor: Has a plan. The plan is a spreadsheet. The spreadsheet is of you.
manager._attackInterval: 2.0 AND NOT THE BRIEF'S 1.6, for the third time a brief has asked for a rank-and-file attacker over 12 damage a second. At 24 damage every 1.6s that is 15.0 a second and three of them kill Cory in 8.0s, against armor.test.ts's ten-second floor; 2.0 is exactly 12.0. The 24 stays because it is the number a player watches land.
manager._displayHeight: DRAWN AT 85 AND NOT THE 92 THE BRIEF ASKED FOR, in art.json. Every tower in the game is 87.1 px tall and content.test.ts holds the rank and file under that, so a 92 px Middle Management would be the only ordinary enemy on the board taller than every building on it. Level 6's Bruiser was asked for at 92 and shipped at 85 for the same reason.

officeDrone.name: Office Drone
officeDrone.flavor: Carries one sheet of paper from nowhere to nowhere. It has been promoted twice.
officeDrone._layer: THERE IS NO `layer` HERE AND THERE MUST NOT BE. An Office Drone is a GROUND UNIT: every tower may shoot it, and putting it on the air layer would make it invisible to the ground-only Mortar and hand the level to whoever drafted the right gun. `glides` is a different question -- what it is out of reach OF, which is things lying on the ground -- and it is the Glider's field, set for the Glider's reason. It hovers and is drawn with a bob; that is art, not a layer.
officeDrone._peanutReward: ZERO, AND THAT IS WHAT STOPS THE CEO BEING AN ECONOMY FAUCET. He summons eight of these over two phases; at any reward at all a player could farm the boss fight for peanuts, which is the opposite of what a boss should pay for.

ceo.name: The CEO
ceo.flavor: Has read the room, optimised the room, and let the room go. Synergy.
ceo._onHealthThreshold:
A LIST, WHICH IS NEW: the field held one object for Batula's roar at 50% and level 8 needed two phases, so it now takes either shape -- one object unwrapped, several as a list, exactly the way `LaneDef.merge` reads. Batula's row is untouched. Each threshold fires ONCE PER ENEMY and they are latched independently, so a boss healed back above 70% does not summon again.
THE CAP IS 6, NOT 8. It counts the drones of THIS boss that are still alive, so the second phase tops the board up to six rather than adding four unconditionally: a player who cleared the first four gets the full second wave, and a player who is drowning in them does not get eight. Four plus four with no cap is a board state nobody chose.
ceo._maxHealth: 8,100, RE-DERIVED AFTER THE LEVEL 8 RE-TOPOLOGY, and the old number and its whole derivation are void. It was 8,500 against a board with ONE entrance on the west and TWO exits, where the Performance Review stood on one of the two exits and buffed 6.1 of 239 enemies a run -- so the 8,500 was measured on a board whose signature mechanic touched one enemy in forty. The level is two entrances and one exit now, both mouths feed the beam, 82.5 enemies a run are buffed, and every number had to be measured again. THE TABLE AT 120 SEEDS: 6,500 -> 50%, 7,500 -> 47%, 7,900 -> 43%, 8,100 -> 40%, 8,300 -> 37%, 8,500 -> 36%, 9,500 -> 26%, 10,500 -> 18%. See reports/2026-09-13-level-8-retopology.md.
ceo._damage: 0 AND `blockable: false`, like every other standing boss: he walks through the line rather than being held by it, so there is nothing for him to hit. The fight is the health and the two summon phases, which is what the brief asks for -- the difficulty of this level is the 3,646 px route and the gate, not a boss with a gimmick.

hatchback.name: Rust Bucket
hatchback.flavor: Held together by bumper stickers and optimism. Mostly the stickers.
hatchback._peanutReward: 26, not the brief's 10, AND THE LEVEL DOES NOT WORK WITHOUT IT. Measured: at the brief's rewards the scripted player had 3 towers by wave 6 where level 6 had 18, and level 7 soaked at 0/30 at every rank-and-file health from 40% to 100% of the brief's. Three independent lanes need roughly three times the guns of one, and each tower only gets 1.9 seconds on a passing Rust Bucket against level 1's 4.1, so the board has to come up fast or it never comes up. 26 is the Scrapper's number on level 6, which is the closest level in shape.
hatchback._maxHealth: 60, not the brief's 85. A tower at this board's standoff covers about 238 px of the lane beside it, which is 1.9 seconds of a 125 px/s car and about 32 damage -- so at 85 the FIRST tower a player builds cannot kill anything at all, and the level opened 0/30. At 60 it dies to two passes, which is roughly what level 1's Late Filer costs its opening tower.

musclecar.name: Roadrager
musclecar.flavor: Has somewhere to be. Has always had somewhere to be. Will not say where.
musclecar._speed: 190 px/s, THE FASTEST THING IN THE GAME, past Baby Frank's 172. The brief's starting value was 150 and it could not stay there: tests/rules.test.ts asks that a level's `fast` role be more than 1.5x its `basic`, and 150 against the Rust Bucket's 125 is 1.20x -- a fast enemy that is not fast. The choice was to slow the Rust Bucket to 95 or to speed this up, and a muscle car on a motorway outrunning a baby Frankenstein is the answer that matches what the level is; slowing the basic would have made level 7's rank and file the slowest in the game for no reason but a ratio. tests/level6.test.ts records the new ranking rather than being relaxed, which is what it already did when level 8's Intern took third place.
musclecar._armor: ZERO, not the brief's 5. Same rule, same test: a `fast` enemy may not carry armour at all -- `${level}: ${e.name} is fast AND armoured` -- because the point of the role is that it gets past you rather than through you. The 5 points are given back as speed.
musclecar._attackInterval: 1.2s, not the brief's 0.9. tests/rules.test.ts holds Cory to ten seconds against three of the heaviest rank-and-file attacker at once, and his 360 health over a block capacity of 3 puts the ceiling at exactly 12.0 damage a second. 14 over 0.9 is 15.6 and would have left him 5.3 seconds. The briefed DAMAGE is kept and the interval carries the change, because 'hits hard' is the character and 'hits often' is the arithmetic.
musclecar._peanutReward: 55, scaled with the Rust Bucket's. See its `_peanutReward`.
musclecar._maxHealth: 100, not the brief's 190. At 190 px/s a Roadrager is inside a tower's reach for 1.25 seconds -- 21 damage -- so 190 health is nine tower passes and nothing on this board kills one before wave 9.

van.name: The Delivery
van.flavor: Two lives' worth of parcels and not one of them is yours.
van._attackInterval: 1.7s, not the brief's 1.4, for the Roadrager's reason: 20 over 1.4 is 14.3 damage a second against a 12.0 ceiling. See `musclecar._attackInterval`.
van._peanutReward: 90, AND IT IS A CEILING RATHER THAN A CHOICE. tests/rules.test.ts asks every boss in the game to pay at least ten times the best ordinary kill, and the smallest boss purse is the Politician's 900 -- so no rank-and-file enemy anywhere may pay more than 90 without retuning level 1. The soak wanted more: level 7 is three roads with a 1400 px lane, so it needs about three times the towers of a one-road level and it needs them early, and at the brief's 32 the board never came up at all. 90 is as far as the rule allows and it was enough.

cargoRed.name: Red Runaway
cargoRed.flavor: Rolled off the trailer and kept going. Nobody signed for it.
cargoRed._cargo: FOUR ROWS, IDENTICAL BUT FOR THE SPRITE, and they are four rows rather than one because the finale is about RECOGNITION: the player has spent the whole boss fight looking at a red, a blue, a yellow and a green car strapped to that trailer, and what comes off it has to be those four cars. One row with a random sprite would put two yellows on the road half the time and would be a different, worse joke. Their stats are the same to 0 in every field, which tests/level7.test.ts asserts, so nothing about which colour you shoot first matters.
cargoRed._peanutReward: ZERO, AND THAT IS WHAT STOPS THE FINALE BEING A PAYDAY. Four cars at the Delivery's 32 peanuts would hand a player 128 peanuts at the exact moment there is nothing left to spend them on, which is not a reward, it is a number going up on a screen nobody is reading. The same rule the Office Drone gets on level 8 and for the same reason.
cargoRed._livesCost: 2 EACH, SO THE FINALE IS WORTH EIGHT LIVES IF ALL FOUR GET OUT. That is the risk Eli raised and Cory kept: a Transporter killed on top of the exit puts four cars on top of the exit. There is no clamp, no minimum spawn distance and no grace period, deliberately -- killing it early is what buys the room. The report measures how often that actually decides a run.
cargoRed._attackInterval: 1.55s, not the brief's 0.8. 18 over 0.8 is 22.5 damage a second, which is nearly double the 12.0 ceiling tests/rules.test.ts sets on the rank and file -- four of these arriving at once on top of the hero is exactly the board state that rule exists for, and it would have left Cory 5.3 seconds. All four carry the same number, as they carry the same everything.

cargoBlue.name: Blue Runaway
cargoBlue.flavor: Rolled off the trailer and kept going. Nobody signed for it.

cargoYellow.name: Yellow Runaway
cargoYellow.flavor: Rolled off the trailer and kept going. Nobody signed for it.

cargoGreen.name: Green Runaway
cargoGreen.flavor: Rolled off the trailer and kept going. Nobody signed for it.

bladeRig.name: The Blade Rig
bladeRig.flavor: Eighteen wheels. Forty blades. No brakes, and no interest in yours.
bladeRig._unstoppable: THREE FLAGS SAYING ONE THING: it cannot be held, slowed or stopped. `blockable: false` and `slowable: false` already existed; `stunnable: false` is new and is the reason it had to be -- the Politician and the Rainbow Reaper are both unblockable and unslowable and both perfectly stunnable, because on those fights a 0.6s Amendment is a reward for good play. Here it is the off switch. `glides: true` is the fourth: nothing lying ON the ground touches it. LEVEL 7 HAS NO GROUND HAZARD for it to ignore -- there is no acid, no scorch and no rules block that lays anything down -- so today that flag is a statement rather than a behaviour, and it is here so that it stays true the day one is added rather than becoming a bug then.
bladeRig._damage: ZERO DAMAGE AND A 99s INTERVAL, which is the Rooster's and the CEO's row and means the same thing: those two fields are what an enemy does to whatever is HOLDING it, and nothing ever holds this. What it does to the player's units is `bladed`, which is the other direction -- a cost for standing where it is driving, paid by anything of the player's in the way. The numbers are level7.json's `blades`.
bladeRig._tier: `tier` IS elite AND `role` IS boss, the Vampire Lord's split and for his reason: `tier` is what the rules read, and a `boss` tier takes the health bar across the top of the screen. The Rig appears TWICE and is not the level's boss; the Transporter is. `role` is what a reader and the draft read, and this is a mini boss.
bladeRig._maxHealth: 600, AND IT IS SOAKED RATHER THAN BRIEFED. The sensitivity table at 40 seeds: 400 -> 40%, 800 -> 35%, 1200 -> 35%, 1600 -> 28%. It is small because this board's lanes are short: at 45 px/s the Rig is inside one tower's reach for 5.3 seconds, and on its second appearance it walks the SOUTH highway, where only 11 of the 22 pads can reach it at all. Do not compare it to another level's boss -- see map_level7.json's `_buildSpots`.

transporter.name: The Transporter
transporter.flavor: Four cars on the back and every single one of them is going to be a problem.
transporter._finale:
IT DOES NOT DIE, IT UNLOADS. At zero health the Transporter vanishes in a puff and the four cars on its trailer come off AT THE PLACE IT DIED, in its own lane, already rolling -- one red, one blue, one yellow, one green, which are the four painted on the art the player has been shooting for the last minute. `holdsWave: true` is what makes the level wait for them: everywhere else a summoned child is kept out of the wave-over count on purpose, and here the children ARE the end of the level.

WHERE IT DIES IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Kill it early and four cars have most of a highway left to walk past your guns. Kill it on the exit line and four cars are on the exit line, and eight lives go with them. Eli raised that during design and Cory decided the risk stays, because it is what makes killing it early matter. THERE IS NO CLAMP, no minimum spawn distance and no grace period, and adding one would be reverting the decision rather than fixing a bug.

`spacingPx: 44` strings them back along the lane the way a trailer actually empties -- the FIRST car is still exactly on the death point, so the worst case is not softened -- and `emergeSeconds: 0.35` is the beat between one and the next. Both are here rather than in the code so they can be tuned without a build.
transporter._slowable: SLOWABLE, unlike the Blade Rig and unlike the CEO. It is the opposite kind of fight: the Rig's identity is that nothing stops it, and this one's is WHERE it stops. A player who slows the Transporter is buying exactly the thing the finale is about -- more road between the wreck and the exit -- and taking that away would make the only decision in the fight unavailable.
transporter._peanutReward: 2000, the largest in the game, and it is paid on a wave that has four cars still to come. That is deliberate: it is the one boss payout a player can still spend.
transporter._maxHealth: 3,000, SOAKED AND NOT BRIEFED, and it is a number about THIS board and no other. The table at 40 seeds, routed down the middle: 650 -> 68%, 1500 -> 68%, 2500 -> 57%, 3500 -> 38%. Routed down the SOUTH highway instead -- 11 pads bearing rather than 20, and 189 px at the end that nobody reaches -- the same band costs 650, which is less than the wave 8 mini boss's and reads as a finale weaker than the wave before it; that is why it is not routed there. Its ARMOUR was swept too and the table came back flat (0 -> 43%, 6 -> 45%, 12 -> 43%, 18 -> 43%), so health is what controls this fight and armour is flavour. Full numbers in reports/2026-09-13-level-7.md.

packet.name: Packet Loss
packet.flavor: Carrying something important somewhere important. Has not checked which.
packet._level9: LEVEL 9, AI OVERRIDE PART 1. Four regulars and four mini bosses, and every display name is HERE and nowhere else -- the wave table names ids, the HUD reads `name` off this row, so renaming one of these is one edit in one place. Working names: Cory and the kids get the last word. ARTFACING COMES FROM reports/2026-09-12-level-9-10-art-manifest.md, which measured it off the pixels with a control -- lvl9-miniboss-nopilot carries the readable words NO PILOT and they came out forwards, proving the renderer does no flipping. An earlier external inspection gave six of these backwards. THE WHOLE CAST FACES RIGHT. THREE OF THEM MUST NEVER BE MIRRORED whatever this field says: the No-Pilot carries readable text, the Perplexed IS a question mark, and the Hat is asymmetric. Level 9 runs left to right and the trace never doubles back into a leftward heading long enough to flip anything, so `artFacing: right` on those three means the mirror never fires -- see systems/Facing.ts.
packet._peanutReward: THE FOUR REGULARS PAY ABOUT 0.15 PEANUTS PER POINT OF THEIR OWN HEALTH, which is not a taste decision: tests/content.test.ts holds a whole wave table to at least 0.13 income per point of health, because a board that cannot be built fast enough to keep up is not a difficulty setting. They were written at half this and the table came out at 0.108. Level 8 runs at 0.175 and level 6 at 0.299.
packet._speed: 142 AND NOT 145 OR 150. It is far and away the fastest thing on level 9 -- the next is the Data Bug at 88 -- and it deliberately sits UNDER level 8's Intern at 145, because tests/level6.test.ts records the four fastest things in the game by name and a new level is not a reason to rewrite that list. The four are Baby Frank at 190, the Musclecar at 172, the Sprinter at 150 and the Intern at 145.

corrupt.name: Corrupted Entry
corrupt.flavor: Something in here used to be a customer record. It is doing its best.
corrupt._damage: 13 OVER 1.1 SECONDS = 11.8 DPS, AND 12.0 IS THE CEILING FOR ANYTHING RANK AND FILE. tests/armor.test.ts measures Cory against three of the highest-DPS non-boss enemy in the game and holds him to ten seconds in front of them, which with his 360 health and block capacity 3 puts the cap at exactly 12.0. Five enemies across levels 4 to 8 sit on it; this was written at 14/1.1 and Cory came out at 9.4 seconds.

dataBug.name: Data Bug
dataBug._glides: IT HOVERS, AND IT IS NOT AN AIR UNIT. `glides` is the Glider's flag from level 5 and it is a LOOK plus a small cost, not a layer: the sprite bobs, its shadow is drawn under its body rather than under a foot, and every tower in the game can still shoot it. `layer: "air"` would have been the other thing -- a unit only some towers can reach -- and level 9 does not have an anti-air tier to build around it. See the note on `glides` in types.ts.

serverWalker.name: Server Walker
serverWalker.flavor: Four legs, sixty-four gigabytes, and no plan beyond forward.
serverWalker._note: THE FOURTH REGULAR, NOT A FIFTH MINI BOSS, despite the source file being called lvl9-miniboss-server.png. It is the heaviest of the four things that fill the waves between the gauntlet's four fights -- the Middle Management of this level -- and the art key is `enemy-server-walker` because that is what it is. The source PNG keeps its name.
serverWalker._armor: 14, WHICH IS THE CAP THE WHOLE GAME HAS. It was written as 18 and tests/content.test.ts rejected it: Cory's Depreciation strips at most 7 armour and the test holds that to at least half of the heaviest armour in the cast, so 14 is the most anything in this game may ever carry. Middle Management has had it since level 8 and this is the level 9 equivalent. Worth knowing before anybody writes a tougher wall.
serverWalker._damage: 22 OVER 2.0 SECONDS, AND THE CEILING IS THE HERO. tests/armor.test.ts measures Cory against three of the highest-DPS NON-BOSS enemy in the game and holds him to ten seconds of standing in front of them; this was written at 26 and he lasted 9.2. 11 dps is the most anything rank-and-file may ever do.
serverWalker._peanutReward: 90 IS THE CEILING FOR ANYTHING THAT IS NOT A BOSS, and it is a hard one: tests/rules.test.ts makes every boss purse at least ten times the best ORDINARY payout, and the smallest boss purse in the game is the Politician's 900. This was written at 135 and it demanded 1350 from every boss on every level -- one level 9 row retuning four earlier levels. Level 4's Glitch Bug already sits on the 90.

hatGtt.name: HAT-GTT
hatGtt.flavor: Generative Trained Transformer. It transformed. It is a hat.
hatGtt._gauntlet: THE GAUNTLET: four fights in one level, in this order -- HAT-GTT, CANCER, NO-PILOT, PERPLEXED. THE FIRST THREE ARE THE BLADE RIG'S SHAPE EXACTLY, which is what a mini boss is in this game: `role: boss` so every rule that must not touch a boss does not touch them, `tier: elite` so the level still fields exactly one boss, `blockable: false` so nothing parks them, and their wave names them as its `boss` so the HUD announces them. PERPLEXED IS `tier: boss` because it is the last fight of the level and something has to be: tests/rules.test.ts holds every wave table to exactly one boss sprite, which is the rule that stops a level quietly fighting two, and level 9 is not the level to relax it in. In the fiction all four are mini bosses and Vlaude is not a combatant at all. NONE OF THEM GETS A NEW COMBAT SYSTEM. Every ability is a system that already shipped, already has tests, and -- this is the part that matters -- is ALREADY RUN BY tools/soak/Sim.ts, so the win rate the soak reports is the fight the player has. HEALTH IS SOAKED AGAINST LEVEL 9'S BOARD AND NO OTHER. Fifteen pads, three of which cannot reach the route at all at the shortest tower range and only three of which cover two passes of it: this board holds LESS effective DPS than level 8's nineteen, so a number carried across from the CEO would be far too high. See reports/2026-09-13-level-9.md for the sensitivity tables.
hatGtt._note: WALL OF TEXT IS `flame`, and that is the whole implementation. systems/Flame.ts is level 6's Rooster breath and it is not a rooster-shaped thing: it is a TELEGRAPHED CORRIDOR ahead of a boss that hurts what is standing in it and leaves the towers it crossed firing slower for a few seconds. Point its `fx` at fx-wall-of-text, put the numbers in level9.json, and document strips slam forward down the lane and bury a row of guns in paperwork. The telegraph is not decoration -- an unavoidable hit with no warning reads as the game cheating, which is why that module has one and why this does not get to skip it. REGENERATE IS REAL HEALTH, not a flourish. `regen` heals 420 off a 3200 pool once its health is under three quarters, every 9 seconds, and plays fx-hat-regenerate OVER the hat -- the effect sheet is the fragments reversing inward into a repair ring, and it is drawn on the hat rather than instead of it, so a second hat never appears. A player who leaves it alone is fighting an 3200 pool that keeps refilling; the answer is concentrated damage, which is the opposite of what CANCER asks for next. THE TWO STATES ARE THE JOKE. -a and -b are the same hat at different tilts and the transformation changes almost nothing. `regen` swaps to `enemy-hat-gtt-b` while it heals and back afterwards, which is the only time the second state is used and the only visual difference there is meant to be.
hatGtt._stunnable: NOT DECLARED, AND THE BLADE RIG'S `stunnable: false` IS NOT COPIED. tests/level7.test.ts holds the Rig to being the only thing in the game that cannot be held, slowed or stopped -- that is its whole character -- and four more of them would take the one thing that makes it different. Level 8's CEO does not declare it either. These four are `blockable: false` and `slowable: false`, which is the boss default.
hatGtt._livesCost: SIX AND SEVEN FOR THE THREE MINI BOSSES, TWELVE FOR THE BOSS, and the gap is a gate rather than a feel: tests/wave.test.ts holds every non-boss row under the CHEAPEST boss in the game, so three things carrying `tier: elite` at 8 and 9 put the whole roster in breach. Level 7's Blade Rig -- the same shape as these three -- costs 6. PERPLEXED at 12 sits between the Politician at 10 and The Devil at 12, and under the 20 lives a run starts with, because a boss escape that ends the run on its own hides the rule instead of teaching it.
hatGtt._soaked: 650 HEALTH AND 130 A REPAIR, both off the soak and both a long way down from where they started. HAT-GTT opened at 1980 health with a 420 repair every 9 s and got out of 40 runs in 40 -- not a fight, a toll. The first two guesses at why were both wrong and both measured: dropping its armour from 10 to 4 moved the win rate by one point, and dropping its health to 1150 by three. What actually holds it up is the REPAIR. Level 9's board is only two or three towers deep at wave 4 and the whole board puts about 1,500 damage on it over its walk; at 1980 + ~1200 healed it could not be killed by any draft. At 650 + ~490 healed it dies in about two thirds of the runs that reach it, which is a first mini boss. See the sensitivity table in reports/2026-09-13-level-9.md: `regen.heal` moves the level nine points across its range and `armor` moves it by noise.
hatGtt._armor: 4, AND THE TABLE FOR IT IS FLAT. 0, 2, 4, 8 and 12 give 42, 41, 40, 43 and 41 per cent over 120 seeds -- noise. It is not that armour does nothing: the escapes climb 38, 41, 47 straight through. What does not move is the WIN RATE, because a run that loses six more lives at wave 4 is a run that does not reach wave 16, and wave 16 is where this level is decided. 4 is chosen on feel, not on the win rate: the first mini boss should reward the cheap early towers rather than floor them at `Math.max(1, damage - armor)`.

cancer.name: CANCER
cancer.flavor: A crab made of stars, dragged out of a sky nobody was using.
cancer._note: THE CONSTELLATION CLAW IS `towerDisable`, the Rainbow Reaper's cast, with the claw sheet landing on the target instead of a bolt leaving the caster. systems/TowerDisable.ts gives it the cooldown, the choice of target -- the most expensive tower in range -- the 1.4 second telegraph that makes the choice visible before anything resolves, and the rule that a caster killed mid-windup lands nothing. `landFx` is the one field added for level 9: the claws close ON the tower from above, so no bolt is drawn and the ring is the whole warning. SIX SECONDS IS A LONG DISABLE and it is the point of this fight: CANCER takes the single gun you invested in and turns it off for six seconds at a time from 300 px away, which asks for a spread board -- the exact opposite of the concentrated damage HAT-GTT asks for. Two fights, two answers, and a player who solved the first one by stacking one corner walks into the second one with the wrong board. NO MEDICAL REFERENCE AND NO ZODIAC TEXT, in the name, the flavour or the art. It is a crab made of stars.
cancer._armor: 14 for the same reason serverWalker carries 14 -- see its note. The heaviest armour in the game, shared with the Middle Manager.
cancer._soaked: 3100 HEALTH, and its armour table is flat for HAT-GTT's reason -- 6, 10, 14, 18, 22 give 43, 44, 40, 42, 40 per cent while its escapes climb 21, 28, 40. The dial that moves this fight is the CLAW: `towerDisable.cooldown` takes the level from 36% at 3.5 s to 44% at 20 s, and `duration` from 44% at 1 s to 37% at 12. 7.5/6.0 sits in the middle of both and is measured, not chosen.

noPilot.name: NO-PILOT
noPilot._note: THE CHARGE IS `bladed`, level 7's Blade Rig, and it is the right system for it rather than a near one: a continuous cost for standing where this thing is walking, paid by whatever is in the way, with nothing to block and nothing to aim. An out-of-control vehicle does not pick a target -- that is what makes it out of control -- and systems/Blades.ts already says so. level9.json's `blades` block points its art at fx-nopilot-crash, so the warning lights, the impact and the skid play AT THE CONTACT POINT and the damage lands there in the same frame. IT IS THE FAST ONE. 58 px/s against the other three at 24-26, and `blockable: false` on top, so it is through a stretch of board before a slow tower has fired twice. The answer is rate rather than damage, which is a third different board again.
noPilot._soaked: 3400 HEALTH, BUT SPEED IS THE DIAL. Health moves the level from 42% at 2600 to 33% at 4200; SPEED moves it from 43% at 34 px/s to 28% at 82, and 58 is already the fastest thing in the game. It walks the LONG arm -- see the note on wave 12 in waves.level9.json -- because on the short one it reached the door in 29 seconds past a third of the guns and walked out of 40% of runs. Its blades are worth 83 damage a run to the player's own units, which is real and small; the level does not rest on them.

perplexed.name: PERPLEXED
perplexed.flavor: Cites four sources. Two of them are each other.
perplexed._note: THE CITATION STORM IS THE SAME CAST AS CANCER'S AND THE NUMBERS ARE THE MECHANIC. That is deliberate and it is said plainly rather than dressed up: one system, two settings, and they play completely differently. CANCER takes one gun away for six seconds every seven and a half from 300 px; PERPLEXED takes whatever is nearest for 1.8 seconds every 2.6 from 210 px. The first is a hole in your board. The second is a board that will not hold still -- guns flicker off and on around it and the answer is more of them rather than better ones. A BURST AND A SHORT DISRUPTION, which is what the brief for it asks for, built out of what the engine already shows clearly: the ring, the citation sheet landing on the target and the stunned marker. NO NEW STATUS SYSTEM was invented for the joke.
perplexed._soaked: 8100 HEALTH, AND THIS IS THE NUMBER THAT SETS THE LEVEL. Every other dial on this board moves the win rate by a few points or by noise; this one moves it from 52% at 7300 to 29% at 8900, and its CITATION STORM moves it further than that -- `towerDisable.duration` at 5.0 s gives a 4% win rate and at 0.5 s gives 55%. 1.8 s and 2.6 s apart is a board that flickers rather than one that goes dark, which is the joke and is also the only setting that leaves the fight winnable. 30% of all losses are this one taking the last life, which is what a finale should be.

mashBullTourist.name: Gore Guide
mashBullTourist.flavor: Half minotaur, half package holiday. Will charge you, then ask you to take the picture again.
mashBullTourist._facing: RIGHT, read off the rendered art and not assumed. All four mash-ups and all four callbacks are drawn walking left-to-right, which is the direction this lane runs, so none of them is mirrored. The field exists because five level 3 enemies walked backwards for a release when Enemy.ts carried 'the art is drawn facing right' as a blanket rule.
mashBullTourist._damage: 14 OVER 1.25s IS 11.2 DPS, AND THE CEILING IS 12.0. tests/armor.test.ts holds the heaviest NON-BOSS attacker to what Cory can stand in front of for ten seconds with his whole block capacity on him -- 360 health over 3 blockers is 12.0 dps and not a peanut more. Level 8's HR, Consultant and Manager already sit exactly on it, so a level 10 elite cannot be heavier than they are; it is heavier in HEALTH and ARMOUR instead, which is what a final-level elite should be.

mashDroneCameraman.name: Content Drone
mashDroneCameraman.flavor: Filming this for the record. The record is Vlaude's. So is the drone.
mashDroneCameraman._glides: IT HOVERS, LIKE THE GLIDER, and for the same reason it is NOT given a `layer`: a quadcopter that only anti-air can hit would hand the board to whoever drafted the right gun. `glides` says what it is out of reach OF -- things lying on the ground -- and level10.json's `gliding` block says what that costs it. Every tower may still shoot it.
mashDroneCameraman._speed: 140 AND 155, AND THE FLOOR IS 132. tests/rules.test.ts holds the SLOWEST `fast` enemy in a level's cast above 1.5x the FASTEST `basic` one, so that the two roles are different things rather than two numbers. Level 10's basics are level 9's corrupt at 62 and dataBug at 88, so the bar is 88 x 1.5 = 132 and anything under it is a basic wearing a fast's label. The first draft had these at 108 and 116 and failed exactly that, which is the rule doing its job: a quadcopter and a car should outrun the walkers.
mashDroneCameraman._role: FAST WITH ZERO ARMOUR, and the zero is a rule rather than a choice. tests/rules.test.ts requires every `fast` enemy in a level's cast to carry NO armour at all -- the role is supposed to be answered by rate of fire rather than by pierce -- and it requires the slowest of them to beat the fastest `basic` by half again. Level 10's basics are level 9's corrupt (62) and dataBug (88), so the floor is 132. The first draft had this drone at 108 with 3 armour and the Runabout at 116 with 11, which failed both halves: they were armoured mid-speed units wearing a fast label. Both are pure speed now and the Runabout pays for it in health instead.

mashRoosterPhoenix.name: Phoenix Rooster
mashRoosterPhoenix.flavor: Reborn from the ashes of the Sports Complex. Still cannot be reasoned with.
mashRoosterPhoenix._role: ARMOURED, AND THAT PUTS A CEILING ON ITS SPEED. tests/rules.test.ts requires every `armored` enemy to be slower than every `basic` in the same cast and tougher than all of them; level 10's slowest basic is the corrupt at 62, so 58 is under it and 68 -- which is what this row said first -- was not. A phoenix that outruns the walkers is a fast unit, and this level already has two.

mashUnicornCar.name: Rainbow Runabout
mashUnicornCar.flavor: Two mascots in a trench coat shaped like a hatchback.

callbackPolitician.name: The Politician
callbackPolitician.flavor: Recalled from the village. Has prepared some remarks.
callbackPolitician._callback: LEVEL 1'S BOSS, RETURNED, and the first of the four. Rescaled for this board and NOT retuned in behaviour: the tax phases are `politician`'s own, copied unchanged, because the joke is that it is the same fight. Health is down from 4600 because he arrives during phase 3 with Vlaude already on the lane and three more bosses queued behind him, not as a wave-ending boss with the board to himself.
callbackPolitician._tier: ELITE, NOT BOSS, AND ALL FOUR CALLBACKS ARE. This is level 9's shape exactly -- HAT-GTT, CANCER and NO-PILOT carry `role: boss, tier: elite` and only PERPLEXED carries `tier: boss` -- and it is what keeps tests/rules.test.ts's 'exactly one boss' true of this level: the sprite a player sees as THE boss is Vlaude, and the four who come out of the portal are the fight on the way to him. It also lets them drop a Server Nuke, which an elite may and a boss may not.
callbackPolitician._health: 2900, 3300, 3900, 4600 ACROSS THE FOUR, RISING IN THE ORDER THEY ARRIVE, and the rise is forced as well as fitting. tests/content.test.ts requires every non-boss wave to be heavier than the one before it, and waves 13 to 16 are each one callback plus an escort -- so four callbacks of equal health would need the escorts to carry the whole curve, and by wave 16 that is fifty bodies walking past a mini boss. Level 9 answered the same question the same way: its four mini bosses go 650, 3100, 3400, 8100. The fiction is that Vlaude gets better at rebuilding them as he goes.

callbackDevil.name: The Devil
callbackDevil.flavor: Recalled from head office. Still has not read it.
callbackDevil._callback: LEVEL 2'S BOSS. `summons` is `theDevil`'s with the cap down from 6 to 5 and the interval out from 5 to 5.5. HE BRINGS A SECOND SPRITE WITH HIM: `directReport` is a level 2 enemy, and systems/LevelArt.ts closes the enemy set under summoning, so level 10 fetches demon_direct_report.webp because this row names it. That is the mechanism working, not a leak.

callbackUnicorn.name: The Rainbow Reaper
callbackUnicorn.flavor: Recalled from the sports complex. The horn is a rocket launcher now. It was always a rocket launcher.
callbackUnicorn._callback: LEVEL 3'S BOSS. `towerDisable` is `unicornBoss`'s with the cooldown out from 7 to 7.5, and `slowable: false` is kept for the reason enemies.json's `_slowable` gives: its whole fight is a clock, and a permanent slow would turn the clock off.

callbackLich.name: The Glitch Lich King
callbackLich.flavor: Recalled from the conundrum. There is nowhere left to recompile to.
callbackLich._retreats: FALSE, AND THIS IS THE ONE CALLBACK WHOSE BEHAVIOUR HAD TO CHANGE. `glitchLich` on level 4 sets `retreatsWhenDefeated: true`: he leaves the board at zero health and comes back later in the run as `glitchLichReturn`. There is no later on this level and nowhere to retreat to -- he is the last of the four and Vlaude is already on the lane behind him -- so here he dies. Written out rather than left off, because an absent flag and a false one read the same in the data and only one of them is a decision.

vlaude.name: Vlaude
vlaude.flavor: Out of the core, onto the floor, and still explaining why this is what you asked for.
vlaude._thisIsPhaseThreeOnly: THE ONLY VLAUDE ROW THERE IS, and it is the DAMAGED form. In phases 1 and 2 he is not an enemy at all: he is parked off the lane at the crystal core, untargetable, drawn by systems/Vlaude.ts straight from `enemy-vlaude` and `enemy-vlaude-code`. He becomes an Enemy the instant the scripted float puts him on the lane, which is the same instant he becomes targetable -- so 'untargetable' needs no new flag on Enemy and cannot drift out of step with 'is he on the board'.
vlaude._glides: HE HOVERS, which is level 5's `glides` and not a `layer`. A monolith hanging off a bundle of cables is off the ground, so what is lying on it misses -- but every tower that can shoot a Glider can shoot him, which is the brief's own test.
vlaude._livesCost: 19 OF 20, AND IT IS A BACKSTOP RATHER THAN THE RULE. Vlaude reaching the exit ENDS THE RUN -- level10.json's `vlaude.exitEndsRun`, checked in GameScene before a life is deducted -- so this number is never actually charged. It is here because tests/wave.test.ts requires every boss to cost at least 5 lives and fewer than the 20 a run starts with, and that rule is worth keeping honest: if the instant loss were ever removed, the ordinary leak path would charge 19 and the player would have one life left rather than silently winning. The first draft of this row said 99, which passed nothing and would have read as 'you have plenty of lives' to anyone who deleted the flag.
vlaude._health:
36000, DERIVED BY SOAK AGAINST LEVEL 10'S OWN BOARD AND AGAINST NO OTHER. 480 seeds, every seed in normal mode, Cory on every seed -- which is the method SOAK-REPORT.md's published figures use, measured rather than assumed: the same driver returns level 8's published 200/480 as the same integer and level 9's published 40% as 191/480. 192/480 = 40.0%, the middle of the 35-45% band.
THE SENSITIVITY TABLE, 480 seeds each, same method: 30000 -> 52.5%, 34000 -> 45.0%, 36000 -> 40.0%, 38000 -> 36.3%, 42000 -> 30.6%. A coarse 120-seed pass first put the knee between 20000 (85.5%) and 28000 (52.2%), which is where his health first outlasts what twelve pads covering 94.2% of a 3440 px lane can put through him.
IT IS FOUR AND A HALF TIMES PERPLEXED'S 8100 AND THAT IS THE BOARD, NOT THE BOSS. Level 10 funnels every walker past every gun on one long road; level 9 splits its traffic across two arms and three of its fifteen pads cannot reach the road at all. Level 10 fields MORE total wave health than level 9 -- 103,122 against 69,893 -- and still won 98.6% of normal runs at the 9000 this row was first drafted with, which is the same fact from the other side.
WHAT THE NUMBER IS CONDITIONAL ON, AND IT IS THE WHOLE CAVEAT: it was measured with Vlaude WALKING THE LANE FROM THE GATE and with NO MANIPULATION FIRING, because systems/Vlaude.ts is the rules and the scene does not play them yet. It is a survivability figure for the phase 3 walk and it is NOT a win rate comparable to levels 1 to 9. It needs re-deriving the day the six powers land, and the runner cannot answer any of them -- see reports/2026-09-14-level-10.md.
